standard.title: Retell and adapt familiar texts
standard.description: retell and adapt familiar literary texts through play, performance, images or writing
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have encountered and enjoyed literary texts. They have not yet been explicitly asked to retell a story in sequence or to adapt one — changing elements while maintaining its recognisable structure.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can retell a familiar literary text in sequence through play, performance, images or beginning writing, and can adapt elements of it — changing characters, settings or events — while maintaining story structure.

nodes.label: Retelling maintains sequence
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can retell key events from a familiar story in the correct sequence.
nodes.minimum_width: Retell at least three events from a familiar story in order — orally, through drawing, or through sequenced pictures.
nodes.typical_width: Retell familiar literary texts in sequence using oral retelling, drawings or sequenced pictures; include key characters and events; maintain the story's beginning, middle and end.
wider: Retell the same story through two different modes — oral and sequenced pictures — and compare what each mode captures
Use digital tools to sequence images for a retelling and share with the class
Retell a First Nations Australian story with attention to its cultural sequence of events
nodes.hinge_reason: Sequential retelling establishes the structural knowledge of the story that adaptation in Node 3 depends on — students cannot adapt a story while maintaining its recognisable structure if they have not yet internalised that structure through accurate retelling.

response_modes.reason: Sequencing events correctly is a foundational narrative literacy skill — precision matters, and errors (missing events, wrong sequence) propagate into later story writing. Practice across multiple stories builds the habit.

success_criteria: Student can retell at least three events from a familiar story in the correct order.
Student's retelling includes the beginning and ending of the story.

nodes.label: Role-play brings characters to life
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can take on a character role from a familiar text through play or performance, enacting key events.
nodes.minimum_width: Role-play or act out at least one scene from a familiar story, taking on a character role.
nodes.typical_width: Retell familiar literary texts through play and performance; draw and role-play characters or events; maintain character identity and event logic during dramatic play.
wider: Perform a familiar story as a class drama, allocating roles and rehearsing key events
Role-play the same story with different students in each role across multiple performances — discussing how different portrayals affect the story
Dramatise scenes from First Nations Australian literary texts, attending to cultural context and meaning
success_criteria: Student can enact at least one scene from a story in role.
Student maintains the character's identity and the event's logic during play or performance.

nodes.label: Adaptation changes elements while keeping structure
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can adapt a familiar story — changing a character, setting or event — while maintaining its recognisable structure.
nodes.minimum_width: Change one element of a familiar story (e.g. 'What if the bear was a dog instead?') and explain what would be different.
nodes.typical_width: Adapt familiar literary texts by changing characters, settings or events; use play, performance, drawing or digital tools to represent the adaptation; maintain story structure during adaptation.
wider: Adapt the same story into a different setting or cultural context — discussing what changes and what must stay the same for the story to still work
Retell a story from a different character's perspective, adapting events as needed
Adapt a familiar text into a different mode — for example, turning a poem into a picture story or a story into a chant

response_modes.reason: Adaptation requires students to hold the original structure in mind while simultaneously generating changes — coordinating prior knowledge of the text with creative generation. This integration of memory and creativity is the endpoint of this descriptor.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Adapting familiar texts — especially into different cultural contexts or across modes — is a rich creative and analytical activity with genuine opportunities for deeper engagement for advancing students.
success_criteria: Student can retell an adapted version of a familiar story where at least one element has been changed.
Student's adaptation maintains a recognisable story structure — beginning, key events, ending.
Student can explain what they changed and why.
